description: To develop a clear understanding of Java features and object-orientation. To implement useful programs for real-life problem solving using standard object-oriented features like encapsulation, polymorphism, etc. To design and develop robust programs with object-orientation through Strings, packages, inheritance, interfaces, etc. To implement threads, event handling & GUI features for simple programs.

syllabus.title: Java Features and Elementary Programming
syllabus.body: Overview of Java's architecture and the JVM, basic Java program & its structure, primitive data types, concept of abstraction and encapsulation; classes & objects: declarations, use and programming, constructors, this reference; arrays: single & multi-dimension and programming using array of objects.

syllabus.title: Key Features of OOP using Java
syllabus.body: Thinking in classes & objects, polymorphism, method overloading; Strings in Java, StringBuilder & StringBuffer; inheritance, overriding methods, hiding members, the object reference super, chaining constructors using this() and super().

syllabus.title: Additional Features for Object-Orientation
syllabus.body: Programming using interfaces, extending interfaces, interface references, constants in interfaces; defining and using packages, scope rules, accessibility modifiers; overview of the java.lang package, the Object class, the wrapper classes; static members of classes, main() & its arguments.

syllabus.title: Advanced Features of Java
syllabus.body: Exception handling: try, catch, finally, throw, throws, checked and unchecked exceptions, defining new exceptions; multithreading: overview of threads, the main thread, thread creation, synchronization, thread transitions; event handling & GUI: basics of event handling, graphics programming using JavaFX.

outcomes: Write Java programs that solve simple computing problems.
Design & develop programs for real-life problem solving using object-oriented features and incorporate the advantages of OOP over procedural programming.
Write simple thread based & GUI based programs to have an understanding of parallelization & event handling principles.
referenceBooks: Y. Daniel Liang, Introduction to Java Programming, Comprehensive Version, Pearson Education, 12th Ed. or Latest Edition.
Bruce Eckel, Thinking In Java, Pearson Education, Latest Edition.
Cay S. Horstmann & Gary Cornell, Core Java Volume I, Fundamentals, Sun Microsystems Press, Latest Edition.
